fields.meta_description: Build a service request form that routes each request by type, alerts a named person on urgent ones, and gives requesters a request number.
fields.h1: Build a Service Request Form With Routing and Tracking
fields.hero_description: Build a service request form that sends each request to the team that does the work and gives the requester a number to track.
fields.features_heading: What Happens After Someone Hits Submit
fields.features_subheading: Requesters only see the questions and the confirmation email. Everything else is what happens behind the form once a request lands.
fields.feature_1:
Questions that change by request type

A heating request asks how old the furnace is; a streetlight report asks for the cross street. Each request type shows only its own questions, and each answer is its own field.
fields.feature_2:
Routing to the queue that owns the request

The request type or the address a requester gives decides which queue gets the request. Each team then sees only its own requests, with the details and photos already attached.
fields.feature_3:
An alert to one person for urgent answers

You name the answers that make a request urgent, such as no heat or water on the floor. Those requests skip the queue and go to the person on call as an email or Slack alert.
fields.feature_4:
A request number the requester can quote

Every submission gets its own number, emailed to the requester with a copy of the answers. When the status changes, the requester gets another email that carries the same number.
fields.feature_5:
A dashboard of open requests by age

The dashboard lists every open request with its owner and the number of days it has waited. Filter it by team or by location to see which queue is falling behind this week.
fields.feature_6:
Code export to your own GitHub

On paid plans, Emergent exports the full code of the form and its dashboard to your own GitHub repository. Every part of the app can then be read and changed outside Emergent.
fields.why_title: Why Run Service Requests on Emergent?
fields.why_description: Requests land in a database you own, and there is no response cap: a storm week that triples the call volume still records every request.

fields.tab_content_1:
No heat means the on-call tech hears first

Brightwater Heating's form asks what is wrong first. Ines Albrecht picks No heat, and her request skips the booking calendar and alerts on-call technician Callum Reyes by email. Any other problem opens the calendar to book a visit. Each request saves as a row in Brightwater's database with its address and photos.
fields.tab_content_2:
Streetlight reports come back with a number

Marlow County residents use one form to reach Public Works. Abena Castellanos picks Streetlight out, enters Larkspur Ave and 9th St, and adds a photo. The app emails her request number SR-20417 and queues the report for the street lighting crew. When the crew closes it, another email follows with the same number.
fields.tab_content_3:
Every mixer under 24 months gets a free repair

Kestrel Kitchen's warranty desk asks for the serial number and purchase date first. A mixer under 24 months old goes to the free repair queue, and anything older gets a repair quote first. Of this morning's 4 requests, 3 went to free repair. Lorenzo Achterberg's mixer is 31 months old, and he gets the quote by email.
fields.tab_content_4:
Category decides which team gets each request

Halden Group runs one service request form for its staff, and the category each person picks decides the queue. Oren Takahashi files a broken desk chair under Facilities, and the facilities channel in Slack gets his request with his floor and desk number. Monday's 14 requests split 8 to IT, 4 to facilities, and 2 to HR.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Service Request Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to a service request form that gives every request an owner, flags urgent ones, and emails requesters a number to track.
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Give every request type an owner
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write down every kind of request people send you and who handles each one. Under each type, note what the person doing the work needs before the first call: the address, the model, a photo. That list becomes your prompt in the next step.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Type a plain-English description of the form: the request types, the questions each one asks, and where each request should go. Emergent builds the form and its database from that prompt. Change anything later with another prompt.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Name a person or a queue for each request type, and add a second rule where location matters, such as one crew per district. A request that matches no rule should land with one named person, never in a shared inbox that nobody watches.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Pick the answers that cannot wait, such as a gas smell or a flooded basement, and choose who gets the alert. Keep that list short: when half of all requests are urgent, the alert stops meaning anything to the person on call.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Choose what the requester gets back
fields.howto_step_5_des: Decide what the requester receives after submitting: a request number, a copy of the answers, and an email whenever the status changes. A number they can quote on the phone saves a search through the inbox when they call back.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Enter five requests from last month, including one urgent case and one that fits no type. Check that each one lands with its owner, that the alert reaches the person on call, and that the requester email carries the request number.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Publish the form on the free tier, or on a custom domain, which uses credits. Put the link on the website, in email signatures, and on every invoice, where customers will look for it the next time something breaks.

faq_plan.q: What is a service request form used for?
faq_plan.ref: What is a service request form used for?

prov.original: What is a service request form used for?

faq_plan.a: A service request form is used to ask a team or a company to do a specific job, and to hand over what they need to do it on the first visit. Employees use one for IT and facilities help, residents for city services, and customers for warranty repairs.

faq_plan.q: How to create a service request?
faq_plan.ref: How to create a service request?

prov.original: How to create a service request?

faq_plan.a: As a requester, open the provider's form or portal and pick the request type closest to the problem. Describe it, then keep the request number that comes back after you submit. To build the form your own customers fill in, describe it in a prompt to Emergent's AI form builder, which turns that prompt into the questions and the database behind them.

faq_plan.q: What is an example of a service request?
faq_plan.ref: What is an example of a service request?

prov.original: What is an example of a service request?

faq_plan.a: Resetting a password is one. Atlassian's ITIL guidance says tasks can range from resetting a password to onboarding a new hire. Ordering a new laptop and asking for access to a shared drive are two more from the same desk.

faq_plan.q: What should a service request form ask for?
faq_plan.a: Ask for the requester's name and the best way to reach them, the request type, the location, a short description of the problem, and the hours someone can get in. Then add what each type needs before the first visit. A repair needs the serial number, and a swap of rented equipment needs the contract number from the rental agreement form.
faq_plan.note: B-w-170 2026-10-16: AlsoAsked "Can you give me an example of a service request?" dropped as a same-intent duplicate of slot 3 (QC Q6 P1 on the shared question text; DECISIONS precedent: near-duplicate PAA replaced, e.g. employee-engagement-survey Q5)

faq_plan.q: What is a service request form?
faq_plan.ref: What is a service request form?

prov.original: What is a service request form?

faq_plan.a: A service request form is the form a customer or an employee fills in to ask a provider for one defined job, such as a furnace repair or a new laptop. Each submission becomes a single request with an owner and a status, and it stays open until the job is done. On Emergent, those requests are stored in a database the business owns.

faq_plan.q: Do photo uploads help on a service request form?
faq_plan.hint: What is casa service request form?
faq_plan.a: Yes, for anything physical. A photo of the leak or the model label tells the technician what to bring before the visit. Make the upload optional for requests that involve no object, such as a password reset, and ask for the label as a separate close-up.

faq_plan.q: How many questions should a service request form have?
faq_plan.hint: What is ptde instructor designation services request form?
faq_plan.a: Keep the shared part to five or six questions, then add two or three for each request type. Cut any question the person doing the work never reads. A property manager can go shorter still. If the tenant's phone number is already on file from the tenant screening form, the repair request needs only the unit and the problem, plus a time to get in.

faq_plan.q: How do online plumbing service request forms work?
faq_plan.hint: How online plumbing service request forms work?
faq_plan.a: An online plumbing service request form collects what is wrong, where, and how bad it is before anyone picks up a phone. Ask whether the water is shut off, where the leak is, and when someone can let the plumber in, and ask for a photo of the fixture. An app built on Emergent can also push each request into the scheduling tool the plumber already uses, through that tool's API.

faq_plan.q: How do you create a service request form in a service desk platform?
faq_plan.hint: How to create a service request form in servicenow?
faq_plan.a: In ServiceNow, you build it as a record producer, a specific type of catalog item that lets end users create task-based records, such as incidents, from the service catalog. The questions are catalog variables, which gather information from the user. Each variable can map to a specific field on the record producer's table.

faq_plan.q: Should every team share one service request form?
faq_plan.a: Share one form when the same people ask several teams for help, and let the request type pick the team. Keep a separate form for requests that carry private details. A reasonable accommodation request form, for example, should reach HR alone and never sit in a queue that facilities or IT can read.

plan.angle: The top 10 for service request form is templates and blank PDFs (Smartsheet, Cognito, Jotform, Ninja Forms, two county public works PDFs, a college IT procedure, a ServiceNow portal, an Adobe explainer): each hands over a fixed set of fields and stops at submit. This page shows what happens after submit, which is where a service request succeeds or stalls: the request type decides the questions and the team, urgent answers alert one named person, the requester gets a request number and status emails, and every request is a row in a database the team owns. The four tabs are four real kinds of provider (a heating company, a county public works department, an appliance maker's warranty desk, an internal service desk), and the FAQ answers the definitional searches plus the build questions a provider asks (what to ask, how many questions, photos, one form or several, service desk catalog items).
